why: T54 (R117/R118): the user asked for T-Auto/dsh-ops to be evaluated for internalisation. R117 measured the payloads at ~127 MB, so the repository pins the upstream artifacts instead of vendoring their bytes; the payloads are installed into a profile's node_modules like every other plugin and must be checked against these integrity values before a mount is allowed.

upstream.name: @dsh-ops/bash-win32-x64
upstream.note: R124: fetched with curl (npm pack had ended in ECONNRESET twice in R117). The downloaded tarball hashes to exactly the integrity pinned from registry metadata, so the metadata-sourced pin was correct - the one claim that needed bytes to check is now checked.

platform.why: the package declares os=[win32] cpu=[x64]; our client ships for Windows and this repository's gates run there

license.obligation: Apache-2.0 components require carrying NOTICE and PROVENANCE.md with any distribution; this repository is MIT, so a mount recipe must keep those files next to the payload

installScripts.why: npm lifecycle scripts are the supply-chain surface we refuse to run implicitly; dsh-ops declares only status/build/provision/validate/test/verify, none of which npm runs on install

ranges.satisfiedBy: the vendored kernel declares dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1 and cordis 4.0.5-alpha.1; the kernel's compatibility check uses semver.satisfies(..., { includePrerelease: true }) (packages/boot/app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts:77), so both prereleases satisfy these ranges (corrected in R110)

mount.note: the recipe is pinned here as intent; no gate enforces the integrity check yet, and nothing has been mounted in any world or in the live profile

notYetVerified: activation in a throwaway kernel (does it load clean, and does it print any failure line)
instrument decoupling: the pair reading that our own gates are unchanged with it mounted (it injects a prompt section and can publish a bash tool)
the token-savings claim, measured by us (bytes out and tool-call counts with it on vs off)
payload absence at tool-call time (binary.js:378 says BinaryNotFoundError with the remedy `dsh-ops provision`; we have not exercised that path)
